claim: Mouse embryonic stem cells (ESCs) are in vitro counterparts of the pre-implantation epiblast.
source: Mouse embryonic stem cells (ESCs), in vitro counterparts of the pre-implantation epiblast, exhibit dual properties of self-renewal and differentiation (Boroviak et al., 2015; Bradley et al., 1984; Evans and Kaufman, 1981; Martin, 1981).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature (Boroviak et al., 2015; Bradley et al., 1984; Evans and Kaufman, 1981; Martin, 1981).

claim: ESCs exhibit dual properties of self-renewal and differentiation.
source: Mouse embryonic stem cells (ESCs), in vitro counterparts of the pre-implantation epiblast, exhibit dual properties of self-renewal and differentiation (Boroviak et al., 2015; Bradley et al., 1984; Evans and Kaufman, 1981; Martin, 1981).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature (Boroviak et al., 2015; Bradley et al., 1984; Evans and Kaufman, 1981; Martin, 1981).

claim: ESCs can be suspended in a ground state of pluripotency using two inhibitors (2i) of GSK3 and MEK1/2, along with LIF.
source: In contrast, ESCs can be suspended in a ground state of pluripotency, where self-renewal is decoupled from lineage specification, using two inhibitors (2i) of glycogen synthase kinase 3 (GSK3) and mitogen-activated protein kinase kinase (MEK1/2), along with the cytokine leukaemia inhibitory factor (LIF) (Ying et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature (Ying et al., 2008).

claim: The ESC state is maintained by a core network of transcription factors.
source: While it is increasingly clear that the ESC state is maintained by a core network of transcription factors (Chen et al., 2008; Dunn et al., 2014; Ivanova et al., 2006), less is known about how cells progress from this state to lineage specification (Buecker et al., 2014; Kalkan and Smith, 2014; Smith, 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature (Chen et al., 2008; Dunn et al., 2014; Ivanova et al., 2006).

claim: Loss-of-function screens have highlighted a multi-layered machinery that dismantles the naïve state transcription factor network.
source: Loss-of-function screens have highlighted a multi-layered machinery that dismantles the naïve state transcription factor network (Betschinger et al., 2013; Leeb et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature (Betschinger et al., 2013; Leeb et al., 2014).

claim: The latency period for transition depends on the clearance kinetics of network components.
source: The latency period for transition depends on the clearance kinetics of network components (Dunn et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature (Dunn et al., 2014).

claim: Long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) comprise a large fraction of the transcriptome in diverse cell types and exhibit specific spatio-temporal expression.
source: Within this class, long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) comprise a large fraction of the transcriptome in diverse cell types and exhibit specific spatio-temporal expression (Carninci et al., 2005; Guttman et al., 2009; Necsulea et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature (Carninci et al., 2005; Guttman et al., 2009; Necsulea et al., 2014).

claim: The genomic distribution of lncRNAs is non-random.
source: The genomic distribution of lncRNAs is non-random (Luo et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature (Luo et al., 2016).

claim: A subclass of lncRNAs are divergently transcribed from neighbouring genes and thought to regulate proximal gene expression in cis.
source: A subclass of lncRNAs are divergently transcribed from neighbouring genes and thought to regulate proximal gene expression in cis, either due to the process of transcription (Ebisuya et al., 2008; Engreitz et al., 2016; Martens et al., 2004) or through local lncRNA-protein interactions that recruit regulatory complexes (Lai et al., 2013; Lee, 2012; Luo et al., 2016; Nagano et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature (Ebisuya et al., 2008; Engreitz et al., 2016; Martens et al., 2004; Lai et al., 2013; Lee, 2012; Luo et al., 2016; Nagano et al., 2008).

claim: Knockdowns of a number of lncRNAs have been reported to exert effects on the transcriptome in mouse ESCs.
source: In mouse ESCs, knockdowns of a number of lncRNAs have been reported to exert effects on the transcriptome (Bergmann et al., 2015; Dinger et al., 2008; Guttman et al., 2011; Lin et al., 2014; Sheik Mohamed et al., 2010) and in some cases impair self-renewal (Lin et al., 2014; Luo et al., 2016; Savić et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature (Bergmann et al., 2015; Dinger et al., 2008; Guttman et al., 2011; Lin et al., 2014; Sheik Mohamed et al., 2010).

claim: Knockdowns of some lncRNAs impair self-renewal in mouse ESCs.
source: In mouse ESCs, knockdowns of a number of lncRNAs have been reported to exert effects on the transcriptome (Bergmann et al., 2015; Dinger et al., 2008; Guttman et al., 2011; Lin et al., 2014; Sheik Mohamed et al., 2010) and in some cases impair self-renewal (Lin et al., 2014; Luo et al., 2016; Savić et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature (Lin et al., 2014; Luo et al., 2016; Savić et al., 2014).

claim: A dynamically regulated lncRNA named Ephemeron (Eprn) was identified.
source: We investigated the potential involvement of lncRNAs in transition from the naïve ESC state and identified a dynamically regulated lncRNA (linc1281) that we named Ephemeron (Eprn).
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the manuscript text.

claim: Eprn modulates the dynamics of exit from naïve pluripotency.
source: Execution of pluripotency requires progression from the naïve status represented by mouse embryonic stem cells (ESCs) to a state capacitated for lineage specification. This transition is coordinated at multiple levels. Non-coding RNAs may contribute to this regulatory orchestra. We identified a rodent-specific long non-coding RNA (lncRNA) linc1281, hereafter Ephemeron (Eprn), that modulates the dynamics of exit from naïve pluripotency.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Eprn deletion delays the extinction of ESC identity.
source: Eprn deletion delays the extinction of ESC identity, an effect associated with perduring Nanog expression.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: In the absence of Eprn, Lin28a expression is reduced.
source: In the absence of Eprn, Lin28a expression is reduced which results in persistence of let-7 microRNAs, and the up-regulation of de novo methyltransferases Dnmt3a/b is delayed.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Reduced Lin28a expression in Eprn knockout cells results in persistence of let-7 microRNAs.
source: In the absence of Eprn, Lin28a expression is reduced which results in persistence of let-7 microRNAs, and the up-regulation of de novo methyltransferases Dnmt3a/b is delayed.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data and logical inference from the manuscript.

claim: The up-regulation of de novo methyltransferases Dnmt3a/b is delayed in the absence of Eprn.
source: In the absence of Eprn, Lin28a expression is reduced which results in persistence of let-7 microRNAs, and the up-regulation of de novo methyltransferases Dnmt3a/b is delayed.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Dnmt3a/b deletion retards ES cell transition.
source: Dnmt3a/b deletion retards ES cell transition, correlating with delayed Nanog promoter methylation and phenocopying loss of Eprn or Lin28a.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Dnmt3a/b deletion correlates with delayed Nanog promoter methylation.
source: Dnmt3a/b deletion retards ES cell transition, correlating with delayed Nanog promoter methylation and phenocopying loss of Eprn or Lin28a.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Dnmt3a/b deletion phenocopies loss of Eprn or Lin28a.
source: Dnmt3a/b deletion retards ES cell transition, correlating with delayed Nanog promoter methylation and phenocopying loss of Eprn or Lin28a.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Eprn is rodent-specific.
source: We identified a rodent-specific long non-coding RNA (lncRNA) linc1281, hereafter Ephemeron (Eprn), that modulates the dynamics of exit from naïve pluripotency.
evidence: This claim is supported by sequence analysis and conservation data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Eprn illustrates how lncRNAs may introduce species-specific network modulations.
source: Eprn illustrates how lncRNAs may introduce species-specific network modulations.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the experimental data and discussion in the manuscript.

claim: Post-implantation epiblast derived stem cells (EpiSCs) represent a primed state of pluripotency developmentally downstream of naïve state ESCs.
source: Post-implantation epiblast derived stem cells (EpiSCs) represent a primed state of pluripotency developmentally downstream of naïve state ESCs (Brons et al., 2007; Nichols and Smith, 2009; Tesar et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature (Brons et al., 2007; Nichols and Smith, 2009; Tesar et al., 2007).

claim: 182 genes are over ten-fold differentially enriched in ESCs relative to EpiSCs.
source: We first selected genes that are over ten-fold differentially enriched in ESCs (182 genes) and EpiSCs (131 genes) relative to each other as molecular signatures to represent these two states (Tesar et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is based on analysis of published data (Tesar et al., 2007).

claim: 131 genes are over ten-fold differentially enriched in EpiSCs relative to ESCs.
source: We first selected genes that are over ten-fold differentially enriched in ESCs (182 genes) and EpiSCs (131 genes) relative to each other as molecular signatures to represent these two states (Tesar et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is based on analysis of published data (Tesar et al., 2007).

claim: Serum culture supports a heterogeneous mixture of naïve, primed and intermediate cells.
source: Serum culture supports a heterogeneous mixture of naïve, primed and intermediate cells (Chambers et al., 2007; Kolodziejczyk et al., 2015; Marks et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature (Chambers et al., 2007; Kolodziejczyk et al., 2015; Marks et al., 2012).

claim: Depletion of Stat3, Esrrb, Sox2 and Klf4 led to a decrease in ESC and increase in EpiSC signature.
source: As predicted, depletion of factors that maintain the ESC state, such as Stat3, Esrrb, Sox2 and Klf4, led to a decrease in ESC and increase in EpiSC signature (Figure 1A), while knockdown of Oct4 gave rise to a decrease in both ESC and EpiSC signatures, consistent with its requirement in both states (Niwa et al., 2000; Osorno et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1A and is consistent with known roles of these factors.

claim: Knockdown of Oct4 gave rise to a decrease in both ESC and EpiSC signatures.
source: As predicted, depletion of factors that maintain the ESC state, such as Stat3, Esrrb, Sox2 and Klf4, led to a decrease in ESC and increase in EpiSC signature (Figure 1A), while knockdown of Oct4 gave rise to a decrease in both ESC and EpiSC signatures, consistent with its requirement in both states (Niwa et al., 2000; Osorno et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1A and citations to published literature (Niwa et al., 2000; Osorno et al., 2012).

claim: Oct4 is required in both ESC and EpiSC states.
source: As predicted, depletion of factors that maintain the ESC state, such as Stat3, Esrrb, Sox2 and Klf4, led to a decrease in ESC and increase in EpiSC signature (Figure 1A), while knockdown of Oct4 gave rise to a decrease in both ESC and EpiSC signatures, consistent with its requirement in both states (Niwa et al., 2000; Osorno et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature (Niwa et al., 2000; Osorno et al., 2012).

claim: Eprn showed strong induction within 12 hr of 2i/LIF withdrawal.
source: Eprn showed strong induction within 12 hr of 2i/LIF withdrawal, but decreased subsequently (Figure 1B–D).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figures 1B-D.

claim: Eprn expression decreased after 12 hr of 2i/LIF withdrawal.
source: Eprn showed strong induction within 12 hr of 2i/LIF withdrawal, but decreased subsequently (Figure 1B–D).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figures 1B-D.

claim: Eprn expression was below the detection limit in EpiSCs or mouse embryonic fibroblasts (MEFs).
source: In EpiSCs or mouse embryonic fibroblasts (MEFs), Eprn expression was below the detection limit (Figure 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Northern blotting confirmed the expression of a single Eprn transcript over 1 kb in length.
source: Consistent with the UCSC gene annotation, Northern blotting of total ESC RNA confirmed the expression of a single Eprn transcript over 1 kb in length (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by Northern blotting data shown in Figure 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 1D.

claim: After 24 hr of 2i/LIF withdrawal, Eprn RNA-FISH hybridisation signals displayed predominantly cytoplasmic localisation.
source: After 24 hr of 2i/LIF withdrawal, Eprn RNA-FISH hybridisation signals displayed predominantly cytoplasmic localisation, but from 48 hr onwards the remaining signals were mostly in the nucleus (Figure 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-FISH data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: From 48 hr onwards after 2i/LIF withdrawal, Eprn RNA-FISH signals were mostly in the nucleus.
source: After 24 hr of 2i/LIF withdrawal, Eprn RNA-FISH hybridisation signals displayed predominantly cytoplasmic localisation, but from 48 hr onwards the remaining signals were mostly in the nucleus (Figure 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-FISH data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: In conditions lacking Gsk3 inhibitor CHIRON99021 (CH), Eprn was upregulated.
source: In conditions lacking Gsk3 inhibitor CHIRON99021 (CH), Eprn was upregulated (Figure 1E).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: When transferred to non-supplemented N2B27 medium from PD/LIF, Eprn expression was maintained for 24 hr before declining.
source: When transferred to non-supplemented N2B27 medium from PD/LIF, Eprn expression was maintained for 24 hr before declining (Figure 1F).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: The addition of CH to LIF/serum culture reduced Eprn expression within 24 hr irrespective of the presence of MEK inhibitor PD0325901 (PD).
source: The addition of CH to LIF/serum culture reduced Eprn expression within 24 hr irrespective of the presence of MEK inhibitor PD0325901 (PD) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1G,H).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1G,H.

claim: Eprn is suppressed by CH in self-renewing ESCs.
source: Therefore, Eprn is suppressed by CH in self-renewing ESCs.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the experimental data presented.

claim: During early mouse development, Eprn expression peaked at E4.5.
source: Through analysis of published data, we found that during early mouse development, Eprn expression peaked at E4.5 and was present in both epiblast and primitive endoderm of the mature blastocyst, but absent or low in E5.5 post-implantation epiblast (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A) and later stages between E7 and E17 (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This claim is based on analysis of published data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Eprn was present in both epiblast and primitive endoderm of the mature blastocyst.
source: Through analysis of published data, we found that during early mouse development, Eprn expression peaked at E4.5 and was present in both epiblast and primitive endoderm of the mature blastocyst, but absent or low in E5.5 post-implantation epiblast (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A) and later stages between E7 and E17 (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This claim is based on analysis of published data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Eprn was absent or low in E5.5 post-implantation epiblast.
source: Through analysis of published data, we found that during early mouse development, Eprn expression peaked at E4.5 and was present in both epiblast and primitive endoderm of the mature blastocyst, but absent or low in E5.5 post-implantation epiblast (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A) and later stages between E7 and E17 (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This claim is based on analysis of published data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Amongst adult tissues analysed, Eprn was only detected in kidney.
source: Amongst adult tissues analysed, Eprn was only detected in kidney, and at a much lower level than in ESCs.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Eprn expression is restored upon naïve state resetting from EpiSCs.
source: We also observed that Eprn expression is restored upon naïve state resetting from EpiSCs (Guo et al., 2009; Yang et al., 2010) (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C,D).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2C,D and citations to published literature (Guo et al., 2009; Yang et al., 2010).

claim: Eprn expression is highly specific to ESCs and the early mouse embryo.
source: We conclude that Eprn expression is highly specific to ESCs and the early mouse embryo.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the expression data presented in the manuscript.

claim: LINE and ERVL-MaLR elements are present within the Eprn proximal promoter region (2 kb upstream of TSS).
source: LINE and ERVL-MaLR elements are present within the Eprn proximal promoter region (2 kb upstream of TSS) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by genomic analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: CpG methylation gain at the Eprn promoter was more extensive in the primed E6.5 epiblast (3% to 80%) than the average changes across all promoters (9% to 35%) or the genome (24% to 70%).
source: By examining published data from embryos (Seisenberger et al., 2012; Wang et al., 2014) and ESC progression in vitro (Kalkan et al., 2017), we found that CpG methylation gain at the Eprn promoter was more extensive in the primed E6.5 epiblast (3% to 80%) than the average changes across all promoters (9% to 35%) or the genome (24% to 70%) (Figure 1—figure supplement 2E).
evidence: This claim is based on analysis of published data (Seisenberger et al., 2012; Wang et al., 2014; Kalkan et al., 2017) shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2E.

claim: No major CpG methylation gain at Eprn promoter was present 24 hr post 2i withdrawal.
source: In contrast, no major CpG methylation gain at Eprn promoter was present 24 hr post 2i withdrawal.
evidence: This claim is based on analysis of published data.

claim: Promoter methylation does not initiate Eprn repression, but could contribute to maintain silencing in later epiblast.
source: These data suggest that promoter methylation does not initiate Eprn repression, but could contribute to maintain silencing in later epiblast.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the methylation data presented.

claim: In steady state self-renewal, Eprn loss did not affect the Rex1-GFP profile in either 2i or PD/LIF conditions.
source: In steady state self-renewal, Eprn loss did not affect the Rex1-GFP profile in either case (Figure 2A,B).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2A,B.

claim: Upon transfer to N2B27, Eprn KO cells displayed delayed downregulation of GFP compared to parental cells, measured at 24 hr from 2i culture and 40 hr from PD/LIF culture.
source: Upon transfer to N2B27, Eprn KO cells displayed delayed downregulation of GFP compared to parental cells, measured at 24 hr from 2i culture and 40 hr from PD/LIF culture (Figure 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: By 72 hr, GFP expression was fully extinguished from either starting condition in Eprn KO cells.
source: By 72 hr, however, GFP expression was fully extinguished from either starting condition (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2A.

claim: A transient delay in GFP downregulation in both culture conditions was evident upon Eprn knockdown using siRNAs.
source: A transient delay in GFP downregulation in both culture conditions was also evident upon Eprn knockdown using siRNAs (Figure 2—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2B.

claim: Eprn KO and knockdown cells both gave rise to substantially more undifferentiated colonies than wild type controls in colony forming assays.
source: Eprn KO and knockdown cells both gave rise to substantially more undifferentiated colonies than wild type controls (Figure 2C,D, Figure 2—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2C,D and Figure 2—figure supplement 2C.

claim: Eprn deficiency impairs timely exit from naïve pluripotency.
source: Considered together, these results indicate that Eprn deficiency impairs timely exit from naïve pluripotency.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the experimental data presented.

claim: Lin28a was the most differentially expressed gene between wild type and Eprn KO cells, with Eprn KO cells displaying a twofold reduction in mean expression level.
source: Lin28a was the most differentially expressed gene in the group, with Eprn KO cells displaying a twofold reduction in mean expression level (Figure 2E).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-sequencing data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Lin28a expression is increased when cells transition out of the naïve state in vivo and in vitro.
source: Although Lin28a is commonly considered as a core pluripotency factor, its expression is actually increased when cells transition out of the naïve state in vivo and in vitro (Boroviak et al., 2015; Kalkan et al., 2017; Kumar et al., 2014; Marks et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature (Boroviak et al., 2015; Kalkan et al., 2017; Kumar et al., 2014; Marks et al., 2012).

claim: Eprn KO cells exhibited a higher level of Nanog mRNA.
source: We examined expression of naïve pluripotency transcription factors in Eprn KO cells and found a higher level of Nanog mRNA (Figure 2E, Figure 2—figure supplement 2F).
evidence: This claim is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 2E and Figure 2—figure supplement 2F.

claim: The two-fold reduction in Lin28a mRNA in Eprn KO cells was constant throughout a 24 hr PD/LIF withdrawal time course.
source: The two-fold reduction in Lin28a mRNA in Eprn KO cells was constant throughout this time course (Figure 2F).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Nanog transcript and protein levels remained higher at 16 hr and 24 hr respectively in Eprn KO cells during PD/LIF withdrawal.
source: Conversely, Nanog transcript and protein levels remained higher at 16 hr and 24 hr respectively (Figure 2F, see also 3E,F for protein).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2F and Figure 3E,F.

claim: Upregulation kinetics for Fgf5 were unchanged in Eprn KO cells.
source: Among peri-implantation epiblast markers, upregulation kinetics for Fgf5 were unchanged in Eprn KO cells, but transcripts for Dnmt3a, Dnmt3b and Oct6 remained lower from 16 to 24 hr (Figure 2—figure supplement 2F).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2F.

claim: Transcripts for Dnmt3a, Dnmt3b and Oct6 remained lower from 16 to 24 hr in Eprn KO cells.
source: Among peri-implantation epiblast markers, upregulation kinetics for Fgf5 were unchanged in Eprn KO cells, but transcripts for Dnmt3a, Dnmt3b and Oct6 remained lower from 16 to 24 hr (Figure 2—figure supplement 2F).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2F.

claim: Rescue cells with restored Eprn expression displayed a wild type exit profile as measured by GFP profile 40 hr post PD/LIF withdrawal.
source: The rescue cells displayed a wild type exit profile as measured by GFP profile 40 hr post PD/LIF withdrawal (Figure 2G).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2G.

claim: Lin28a and Nanog expression levels in rescue cells were similar to wild type cells.
source: Lin28a and Nanog expression levels were similar to wild type cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 3C).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3C.

claim: Both wild type and Eprn KO ESCs could be differentiated into EpiSCs.
source: Both wild type and Eprn KO ESCs could be differentiated into EpiSCs using N2B27 supplemented with ActivinA/Fgf2/XAV939 (Sumi et al., 2013) on fibronectin.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data and citation to published literature (Sumi et al., 2013).

claim: In vitro differentiated EpiSCs displayed typical morphology and gene expression irrespective of genotype.
source: Such in vitro differentiated EpiSCs could be stably propagated over multiple passages, and displayed typical morphology and gene expression irrespective of genotype (Figure 2—figure supplement 4A,B).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 4A,B.

claim: Lineage markers were induced in Eprn KO ESCs during neuronal, mesendoderm and definitive endoderm differentiation, with a slight delay for mesendoderm.
source: We also applied neuronal, mesendoderm and definitive endoderm differentiation protocols to Eprn KO ESCs and found that lineage markers were induced, with a slight delay for mesendoderm (Figure 2—figure supplement 4C–E).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 4C–E.

claim: Retarded naïve state exit does not notably impair subsequent lineage commitment capacity.
source: Thus retarded naïve state exit does not notably impair subsequent lineage commitment capacity.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the differentiation data presented.

claim: In Eprn KO cells, Nanog knockdown partially restored downregulation of Rex1-GFP 40 hr after PD/LIF withdrawal.
source: In Eprn KO cells, Nanog knockdown partially restored downregulation of Rex1-GFP 40 hr after PD/LIF withdrawal, and colony formation was reduced to the low level observed in wild type cells subjected to Nanog siRNA (Figure 3A).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Nanog knockdown in Eprn KO cells reduced colony formation to the low level observed in wild type cells subjected to Nanog siRNA.
source: In Eprn KO cells, Nanog knockdown partially restored downregulation of Rex1-GFP 40 hr after PD/LIF withdrawal, and colony formation was reduced to the low level observed in wild type cells subjected to Nanog siRNA (Figure 3A).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Knockdown of Klf4 had no effect on exit kinetics from PD/LIF in either wild type or Eprn KO cells.
source: Knockdown of Klf4 had no effect on exit kinetics from PD/LIF in either wild type or Eprn KO cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Knockdowns of Esrrb, Tfcp2l1 and Klf2 accelerated exit in wild type cells but this phenotype was attenuated in Eprn KO cells.
source: Knockdowns of other naïve transcription factors, Esrrb, Tfcp2l1 and Klf2, accelerated exit in wild type cells but in contrast to Nanog depletion this phenotype was attenuated in Eprn KO cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Simultaneous depletion of Esrrb, Tfcp2l1 or Klf2 together with Nanog largely abolished the effect of Eprn KO on GFP downregulation.
source: Simultaneous depletion of Esrrb, Tfcp2l1 or Klf2 together with Nanog largely abolished the effect of Eprn KO on GFP downregulation (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C,D).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C,D.

claim: Eprn acts, at least in part, via modulation of Nanog expression.
source: These data are consistent with Eprn acting, at least in part, via modulation of Nanog expression.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the genetic perturbation experiments.

claim: In wild type cells, Lin28a overexpression had no significant effect on exit kinetics.
source: In wild type cells, Lin28a overexpression had no significant effect.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: In Eprn KO cells, Lin28a overexpression restored normal transition kinetics.
source: In Eprn KO cells, however, it restored normal transition kinetics (Figure 3B).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Lin28a knockdown phenocopied Eprn loss, delaying exit from naïve pluripotency.
source: Conversely, Lin28a knockdown phenocopied Eprn loss, delaying exit from naïve pluripotency (Figure 3C).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Concomitant knockdown of Nanog and Lin28a abolished the effect of Lin28a knockdown on exit kinetics.
source: Concomitant knockdown of Nanog and Lin28a abolished this effect (Figure 3C).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Lin28a knockdown cells exhibited marginally elevated Nanog mRNA in PD/LIF and persistence at higher levels after 8 hr of PD/LIF withdrawal.
source: Lin28a knockdown cells exhibited marginally elevated Nanog mRNA in PD/LIF and persistence at higher levels after 8 hr of PD/LIF withdrawal (Figure 3D).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Eprn null cultures displayed more cells with high Nanog and low Lin28a expression at the 24 hr time point.
source: At the protein level, Eprn null cultures displayed more cells with high Nanog and low Lin28a expression at the 24 hr time point as quantified by co-immunostaining (Figure 3E,F, Figure 3—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 3E,F and Figure 3—figure supplement 1E.

claim: During early embryo development, expression of Lin28a and Eprn are positively correlated.
source: During early embryo development, expression of Lin28a and Eprn are positively correlated, while Lin28a and Nanog are negatively correlated (Figure 3—figure supplement 1G)(Ohnishi et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is based on analysis of published data (Ohnishi et al., 2014) shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1G.

claim: During early embryo development, Lin28a and Nanog are negatively correlated.
source: During early embryo development, expression of Lin28a and Eprn are positively correlated, while Lin28a and Nanog are negatively correlated (Figure 3—figure supplement 1G)(Ohnishi et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is based on analysis of published data (Ohnishi et al., 2014) shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1G.

claim: Lin28a is genetically downstream of Eprn and may facilitate exit from naïve pluripotency by accelerating downregulation of Nanog.
source: These data are consistent with the proposition that Lin28a is genetically downstream of Eprn and may facilitate exit from naïve pluripotency by accelerating downregulation of Nanog.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the experimental data presented.

claim: ChIRP using probe sets recognising Eprn specifically enriched Eprn RNA.
source: Using this method, we were able to selectively pull down endogenous Eprn RNA (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by ChIRP data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A.

claim: ChIRP did not detect chromatin enrichment at the Lin28a or Nanog promoter regions.

claim: No evidence was found that Eprn functions by chromatin association.

claim: The H3K4me3 modification was reduced at the Lin28a promoter in Eprn KO cells.

claim: Nanog does not appear to be a direct upstream regulator of Lin28a.
source: Therefore, Nanog does not appear to be a direct upstream regulator of Lin28a.

claim: Lin28a is an RNA binding protein with a well-established function in suppressing maturation of let-7 family miRNAs.

claim: Mature miRNA let-7c expression was unaffected after 2i/LIF withdrawal.

claim: let-7c expression is independent of Lin28a.

This observation is in agreement with a recent finding that let-7c-2, the major let-7c isoform expressed in mouse ESCs, bypasses Lin28a regulation due to lack of a GGAG recognition motif in its loop region (Triboulet et al., 2015).

claim: let-7c-2 bypasses Lin28a regulation due to lack of a GGAG recognition motif in its loop region.
source: This observation is in agreement with a recent finding that let-7c-2, the major let-7c isoform expressed in mouse ESCs, bypasses Lin28a regulation due to lack of a GGAG recognition motif in its loop region (Triboulet et al., 2015).

claim: The Lin28a regulated let-7 miRNAs are expressed at higher levels in ESCs in 2i/LIF than in LIF/serum.

claim: Forced expression of let-7g in RGd2 cells resulted in delayed GFP downregulation upon both 2i and PD/LIF withdrawal.

claim: DNA methyltransferases Dnmt3a and Dnmt3b emerged as prime candidates for let-7g targets.

claim: One let-7g target site was predicted in the Dnmt3b 3'UTR.

evidence: This claim is based on bioinformatic prediction using RNA22 tool.

claim: Dnmt3a/3b transcripts are let-7g targets.
source: let-7g reduced luciferase expression by more than 60% relative to scrambled control (Figure 4E), suggesting that Dnmt3a/3b transcripts are indeed let7-g targets.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the luciferase assay data.

claim: Mutant Dnmt3b 3'UTR reporters with the let-7 seed recognition site mutated escaped repression by the let-7g mimic.

claim: A similar acute trend of global DNA methylation acquisition is observed upon naïve ESC withdrawal from 2i.

claim: Dnmt3b depleted cells displayed 18% CpG methylation at scored sites in the Nanog promoter region 1.

claim: Dnmt3a or Dnmt3a/b double knockdown cells showed only around 8% CpG methylation at scored sites in the Nanog promoter region 1.
source: Cells transfected with scrambled control siRNA exhibited 40% CpG methylation at scored sites, whereas Dnmt3b depleted cells displayed 18% CpG methylation and Dnmt3a or Dnmt3a/b double knockdown cells showed only around 8%.

claim: Dnmt3a and Dnmt3b have overlapping roles in mediating de novo methylation at the Nanog proximal promoter.

source: At 8 hr after PD/LIF withdrawal, Nanog mRNA in Dnmt3a and/or Dnmt3b mutants was equivalent to wild type cells in PD/LIF, whereas wild type cells had downregulated Nanog expression by 50% (Figure 5D).

source: Genetic interactions link Eprn with known players in post-transcriptional and epigenetic regulation (Figure 5E). Eprn lies upstream of Lin28a/let-7g and Dnmt3a/3b, and ultimately contributes to timely downregulation of the pivotal naïve transcription factor Nanog.

source: Eprn depletion reduces Lin28a expression, although the molecular mechanism underlying this effect remains unclear.

source: This lncRNA/miRNA/DNA methylation module provides an additional layer in the multi-layered machinery that enforces transition from naïve to formative pluripotency (Acampora et al., 2016; Jang et al., 2017; Kalkan et al., 2017; Kalkan and Smith, 2014; Smith, 2017).

source: Nonetheless, loss of Eprn in PD/LIF resulted in elevated Nanog and delayed transition kinetics.

claim: The lack of ESRRB expression in human pluripotent cells partly explains the reduced impact of Gsk3 inhibition on human naïve state maintenance.
source: This is partly explained by the lack of ESRRB expression in human pluripotent cells (Blakeley et al., 2015; Martello et al., 2012; Takashima et al., 2014; Theunissen et al., 2014), but absence of Eprn may be an additional factor that reduces requirement for Gsk3 inhibition.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature (Blakeley et al., 2015; Martello et al., 2012; Takashima et al., 2014; Theunissen et al., 2014).

claim: Absence of Eprn may be an additional factor that reduces requirement for Gsk3 inhibition in human naïve state maintenance.

evidence: This is a speculative claim based on inference from the experimental data.

claim: A genetic interaction module consisting of a novel lncRNA, proteins and miRNAs is integrated into the multi-pronged molecular machinery that propels mouse ESCs towards lineage competence.
source: In summary, we have mapped a genetic interaction module consisting of a novel lncRNA, proteins and miRNAs that is integrated into the multi-pronged molecular machinery that propels mouse ESCs towards lineage competence.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the experimental data presented.

claim: The fine-tuning effect of Eprn could be representative of lncRNA actions in the regulation of molecular networks.
source: The fine-tuning effect of Eprn could be representative of lncRNA actions in the regulation of molecular networks and illustrative of their potential contribution to species diversification.
evidence: This is a speculative claim based on inference from the experimental data.
